questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with a well-defined hypopigmented patch on his forearm with loss of sensation and a thickened ulnar nerve. Slit skin smear shows no bacilli. Which type of leprosy does this represent?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) presents with a single or few well-defined hypopigmented patches with complete loss of sensation and a thickened peripheral nerve. Slit skin smear is negative (paucibacillary). Granulomas extend right up to the basal layer of epidermis.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with a painful genital ulcer with a soft base, undermined edges, and inguinal lymphadenopathy. The causative organism grows on chocolate agar supplemented with vancomycin. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi, which grows on chocolate agar with vancomycin. It presents with a soft, painful ulcer with ragged undermined edges — contrasting with the painless indurated ulcer of syphilis.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic male presents with a rapidly spreading erythematous plaque on the lower leg with fever and chills. The margin is raised and well-defined. Which condition is most likely?
questions.exp: Erysipelas is a superficial infection involving the dermis and upper subcutaneous tissue, characterized by a well-defined, raised, advancing border — a key distinguishing feature from cellulitis. It is most commonly caused by Group A Streptococcus.

questions.q: A 19-year-old male presents with annular plaques with central clearing on the trunk. KOH mount shows hyphae with arthrospores arranged in a 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Malassezia furfur causes pityriasis versicolor. KOH mount shows short hyphae and rounded yeast cells in a 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. It thrives in lipid-rich environments.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman on hydroxychloroquine for discoid lupus erythematosus complains of difficulty reading. Which investigation is essential for monitoring this complication?
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine can cause irreversible bull's-eye maculopathy. OCT is the most sensitive investigation for early detection of hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity and is recommended for annual screening.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with tense blisters on normal-appearing skin and mucous membrane involvement. Nikolsky sign is negative. Immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid features tense blisters on normal or erythematous skin with negative Nikolsky sign. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ. Autoantibodies target BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230.

questions.q: A 28-year-old HIV-positive male presents with multiple hyperpigmented nodular lesions on the face and trunk that do not blanch on pressure. Biopsy shows vascular proliferation with extravasated red blood cells and spindle cells. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma, associated with HHV-8 infection and immunosuppression (especially HIV), presents with violaceous non-blanching nodules. Histology shows vascular proliferation, spindle cells, and extravasated RBCs with hemosiderin deposits.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with a butterfly-shaped erythema on her face, joint pains, and oral ulcers. ANA is positive (1:320). Which skin finding on direct immunofluorescence is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
opts: IgG at DEJ in lesional skin only
IgG at DEJ in non-lesional sun-protected skin
IgA at DEJ in lesional skin
questions.exp: The lupus band test (LBT) showing immunoglobulin/complement deposits at the DEJ in both lesional AND non-lesional sun-protected skin is most specific for systemic SLE, distinguishing it from discoid LE where only lesional skin is positive.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with pruritic papulovesicles on the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Biopsy shows neutrophilic microabscesses at dermal papillae tips. IgA deposits are found at the BMZ. This patient most likely has which associated condition?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is the cutaneous manifestation of gluten-sensitive enteropathy (celiac disease). IgA deposits at dermal papillae tips and neutrophilic microabscesses are pathognomonic. Dapsone provides rapid relief; gluten-free diet is the definitive treatment.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male presents with scaly silvery plaques on the extensor surfaces and nail pitting. He now experiences DIP joint pain with pencil-in-cup deformity on X-ray. What is the treatment of choice for this arthropathy?
questions.exp: Psoriatic arthritis with destructive DIP involvement (pencil-in-cup deformity) requires disease-modifying therapy. Methotrexate is the first-line DMARD for psoriatic arthritis and also addresses the skin disease. Anti-TNF biologics are used in refractory cases.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the mouth and nose following an upper respiratory tract infection. Tzanck smear is negative. Which is the most appropriate topical treatment?
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes presents with honey-colored crusts. Topical mupirocin is first-line for localized non-bullous impetigo. Retapamulin is an alternative. Systemic antibiotics are reserved for extensive disease.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with a slowly enlarging, pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasias on the nasolabial fold. Dermoscopy shows arborizing vessels. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.exp: BCC on the nasolabial fold — a high-risk H-zone site — is best treated with Mohs micrographic surgery, which provides the highest cure rate and maximum tissue conservation due to real-time margin examination.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on her vulva at 36 weeks gestation. Primary genital herpes is confirmed. What is the preferred management?
opts: Valacyclovir 1g BD for 10 days, then expectant management
Cesarean section at 38 weeks regardless of lesion status
Oral acyclovir 400mg TDS for 10 days, then suppressive acyclovir from 36 weeks
IV acyclovir and immediate cesarean delivery
questions.exp: For primary genital herpes in late pregnancy, oral acyclovir (400mg TDS) treats the acute episode, followed by suppressive acyclovir from 36 weeks to reduce lesion recurrence and neonatal transmission risk. Cesarean delivery is recommended if active lesions are present at onset of labor.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with hypopigmented macules on the trunk with fine scaling. Wood's lamp shows golden-yellow fluorescence. What is the first-line systemic treatment for extensive disease?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor shows golden-yellow fluorescence under Wood's lamp. For extensive disease, oral itraconazole 200mg/day for 5–7 days is preferred. Terbinafine is less effective as Malassezia lacks squalene epoxidase — the target of allylamines.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with sclerotic skin changes, Raynaud's phenomenon, and dysphagia. Matted telangiectasias are noted on the face. Anti-Scl-70 antibody is positive. Which internal organ complication is most common?
questions.exp: In diffuse systemic sclerosis (anti-Scl-70/anti-topoisomerase I positive), interstitial lung disease (ILD) is the most common internal organ complication and leading cause of death. Anti-centromere antibodies are associated with limited SSc (CREST syndrome) and pulmonary arterial hypertension.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman started on dapsone for leprosy develops pallor, jaundice, and hemoglobinuria two weeks later. Which enzyme deficiency makes patients most susceptible to this complication?
questions.exp: Dapsone causes dose-dependent hemolysis and methemoglobinemia. G6PD-deficient individuals are especially vulnerable because they cannot regenerate NADPH to neutralize oxidative stress. G6PD screening before dapsone initiation is recommended.

questions.q: A 60-year-old smoker presents with a firm, indurated ulcer on the lower lip present for 3 months. Biopsy shows islands of squamous cells with keratin pearls invading the dermis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: SCC of the lip is associated with smoking, UV exposure, and HPV. It presents as an indurated ulcer or nodule. Histology shows invasive squamous cell nests with keratin pearl formation. Lip SCC carries higher metastatic risk than cutaneous SCC.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male with IV drug use history presents with painful papules on the palms and soles, arthralgia, and a painless genital ulcer 3 weeks ago. RPR is reactive at 1:32. What is the stage of syphilis?
questions.exp: Secondary syphilis occurs 4–10 weeks after the primary chancre, featuring a diffuse rash (classically on palms and soles), condylomata lata, mucous patches, and systemic symptoms. High RPR titers (≥1:8) are characteristic. Treatment: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose.

questions.q: A 25-year-old atopic woman presents with intensely pruritic lichenified patches in the antecubital and popliteal fossae since childhood. She also has asthma. Serum IgE is markedly elevated. Which cytokines are primarily responsible for the Th2 skewing in atopic dermatitis?
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis is driven by Th2 cytokines — IL-4 (promotes IgE class switching and Th2 differentiation) and IL-13 (causes barrier dysfunction and pruritus). Dupilumab targets the IL-4Rα subunit shared by both receptors and is an approved biologic for moderate-to-severe AD.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with a painless black eschar on the forearm after visiting a farm, with high fever. Gram stain shows large Gram-positive bacilli in bamboo-stick arrangement. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax presents with a painless ulcer with black eschar after animal contact. Bacillus anthracis appears as large boxcar-shaped Gram-positive bacilli in chains. Ciprofloxacin or doxycycline for 60 days is the treatment for cutaneous anthrax (longer course covers potential inhalational spore co-exposure).

questions.q: A 70-year-old immunocompetent woman presents with grouped vesicles in a dermatomal distribution on the right trunk with severe burning pain. What is the drug of choice and treatment window?
opts: Topical acyclovir within 72 hours of rash onset
Oral valacyclovir 1g TDS within 72 hours of rash onset
IV acyclovir 10mg/kg every 8 hours regardless of timing
questions.exp: Herpes zoster is best treated with valacyclovir 1g TDS for 7 days, initiated within 72 hours of rash onset (or any time if new lesions are still appearing). It reduces acute neuritis duration and risk of post-herpetic neuralgia. Famciclovir 500mg TDS is an alternative.

questions.q: A 10-year-old boy presents with diffuse hair loss with grey scales and broken-off hair stumps. Wood's lamp examination shows green fluorescence of the affected area. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes tinea capitis (ectothrix infection) with grey scaling and broken hair. Wood's lamp reveals bright green fluorescence (due to pteridine production). Trichophyton species do NOT fluoresce. Treatment: oral griseofulvin is first-line for tinea capitis in children.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male presents with a dark brown-black irregularly pigmented macule with asymmetric borders measuring 8mm on his back. Dermoscopy shows regression structures and an atypical pigment network. A biopsy is planned. Which biopsy technique is most appropriate?
opts: Punch biopsy at the darkest area only
questions.exp: For suspected melanoma, narrow-margin excisional biopsy (1–3mm margins) encompassing the entire lesion is the standard. This allows accurate Breslow thickness measurement (the most important prognostic factor), guiding subsequent wide local excision margins and sentinel lymph node biopsy decisions.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with malar hyperpigmentation worsening in summer, present since her last pregnancy. Wood's lamp accentuates the pigmentation. What is the first-line treatment?
opts: Triple combination cream (hydroquinone + tretinoin + mild corticosteroid) with sunscreen
questions.exp: Epidermal melasma (Wood's lamp accentuated) is treated with triple combination cream (Kligman's formula: hydroquinone + tretinoin + mild corticosteroid) along with strict broad-spectrum sunscreen. This remains the most evidence-based first-line regimen.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male with lepromatous leprosy on MDT develops painful nodular swellings on the face and limbs with fever. Slit skin smear shows fragmented and granular bacilli with a low morphological index. What reaction is this?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL/Type 2 reaction) occurs in LL and BL leprosy. It is an immune complex-mediated reaction presenting with tender erythematous nodules, fever, and systemic features. Treatment: thalidomide (drug of choice in non-pregnant adults) or prednisolone. Clofazimine has anti-ENL properties.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with crops of clear vesicles on the trunk, face, and scalp in different stages, some umbilicated, with low-grade fever. Tzanck smear shows multinucleate giant cells. What is the causative virus?
questions.exp: Chickenpox (primary VZV infection) presents with crops of vesicles in different stages (polymorphic) in a centripetal distribution (trunk > face > extremities). Umbilicated vesicles on an erythematous base ('dew drops on rose petals'). Tzanck smear shows multinucleate giant cells (Tzanck cells).

questions.q: A patient on isotretinoin for acne has a serum triglyceride of 750 mg/dL at a 6-week follow-up. She is asymptomatic. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Continue isotretinoin and recheck in 4 weeks
Reduce isotretinoin dose by half and add fenofibrate
Switch to doxycycline and continue monitoring
questions.exp: Isotretinoin causes hypertriglyceridemia in up to 25% of patients. Triglycerides >500 mg/dL carry risk of acute pancreatitis. At 750 mg/dL, isotretinoin must be stopped immediately. Resumption may be considered at a lower dose after normalization, with dietary modification and lipid-lowering therapy.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with painless inguinal lymphadenopathy with a 'groove sign' — a groove between two groups of nodes. He recalls a transient genital papule 3 weeks ago. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3. The 'groove sign' (inguinal groove between femoral and inguinal node groups) is pathognomonic. The primary genital papule/ulcer heals rapidly. Treatment: doxycycline 100mg BD for 21 days.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male presents with a firm, flesh-colored dermal plaque on the trunk with a positive 'dimple sign' on lateral compression. Histology shows a storiform pattern of spindle cells with low mitotic rate. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dermatofibroma shows a positive dimple/Fitzpatrick sign — central dimpling on lateral compression. Histology shows a storiform spindle-cell pattern in the dermis. It is CD34-negative and factor XIIIa-positive, distinguishing it from DFSP (CD34-positive, locally aggressive).

questions.q: A patient with extensive alopecia areata (>50% scalp involvement) has failed topical minoxidil and intralesional steroids. Which is the most appropriate next step?
questions.exp: Baricitinib (JAK1/2 inhibitor) is FDA-approved for severe alopecia areata (≥50% scalp hair loss). JAK inhibitors block the IFN-γ and IL-15 signaling pathway driving CD8+ T-cell-mediated hair follicle destruction. Ritlecitinib (JAK3/TEC inhibitor) is another approved option.

questions.q: During a punch biopsy, a vessel is cut and bleeding does not stop with direct pressure. The patient is on aspirin. Which topical hemostatic agent is most appropriate in this outpatient setting?
questions.exp: Aluminum chloride 20–35% in isopropyl alcohol is the most commonly used chemical hemostatic agent in dermatology. It acts by protein precipitation and vasoconstriction. It is preferred over Monsel's solution for punch biopsy hemostasis as Monsel's can cause tattoo-like pigmentation and histologic artifact if the specimen is already retrieved.
